items.headline: HDB unveils plans for up to 18,000 homes at Gillman Barracks and Sunset Way
items.summary: HDB on July 10 published heritage and environmental studies for redeveloping the Gillman Barracks arts enclave and Sunset Way in Clementi, which analysts estimate could yield up to 18,000 flats. Four buildings graded Exceptional will be retained and 30-metre ecological corridors safeguarded, with public feedback open until August 6.

items.headline: Repeat drink-driver and lawyer Steven John Lam is struck off for lying to police
items.summary: Steven John Lam Kuet Keng, 56, was struck off the rolls on July 9 after giving police two false statements claiming another person was driving when he crashed into guard railings on Bukit Panjang Road in 2024. He had earlier been jailed eight weeks, fined S$18,000 and banned from driving for six years.

items.headline: Father jailed 15 months for holding a karambit knife to his daughter's neck
items.summary: A 46-year-old man was sentenced to 15 months' jail after he caned his 11-year-old daughter and pressed an unsheathed karambit blade against her neck for about a minute because she had overslept and missed school. He pleaded guilty to four of 14 charges, and a gag order protects the girl's identity.

items.headline: Thirteen public libraries to close phone-charging stations after safety incidents
items.summary: The National Library Board said on July 8 that charging stations at 13 public libraries will shut from July 27 following a rise in incidents involving unattended devices. Power-bank rentals will be offered as an alternative.

items.headline: India's $50 billion IPO pipeline led by Jio and NSE faces delay as oil spikes
items.summary: CNBC reported on July 9 that about $50 billion of planned Indian listings — including Jio Platforms at roughly $3.5 billion and the National Stock Exchange at about $3.1 billion — risk being shelved after renewed US-Iran conflict lifted oil prices and pressured the rupee.

items.headline: Adani secures nearly $15 billion in a week as its US legal cloud lifts
items.summary: Gautam Adani's group lined up close to $15 billion in commitments in one week, including an $11.5 billion Odisha aluminium venture with Abu Dhabi's IHC and a $1.6 billion Adani Enterprises share sale that was oversubscribed. Bloomberg framed it on July 10 as a comeback after US bribery charges against the group receded.

items.headline: India agrees to supply BrahMos missiles to Indonesia in a third regional deal
items.summary: CNBC reported on July 10 that India will supply its BrahMos and Astra missiles to Indonesia, its third such Indo-Pacific defence agreement, as New Delhi positions itself as an arms supplier to nations wary of China's assertiveness in the South China Sea.

items.headline: India's cricket board to review the T20 team after its tour of England
items.summary: The BCCI said it will convene after the England tour ends on July 19 to assess what it called the T20 side's bad phase, following a run of heavy defeats that cost India the series. Al Jazeera reported the planned review on July 10.

items.headline: Record heatwave pushes the UK power grid to its limit
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Britain's grid operator resorted to emergency measures during the summer's third heatwave, with grid frequency held below its normal level for a record stretch of about 26 minutes. The operator issued a further electricity supply warning on July 8, its third such alert of the summer.

items.headline: UK construction shrinks again in June, denting Starmer's housebuilding pledge
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that the UK construction sector contracted sharply again in June, undercutting the government's flagship homebuilding target amid high interest rates, rising costs and weak demand.

items.headline: Burnham plans to expand the prime minister's grip on economic policy
items.summary: Bloomberg reported on July 9 that Andy Burnham, expected to become Britain's next prime minister, will seek greater No. 10 oversight of economic policy but shelve an immediate break-up of the Treasury, according to a close ally.

items.headline: Typhoon Bavi triggers landslides that kill at least 15 in the southern Philippines
items.summary: Rain from Typhoon Bavi set off landslides that killed at least 15 people and left nine missing across Mindanao on July 10, with 10 dead in Sarangani, where earthquake-weakened soil gave way, and five more killed in Lanao del Sur.

items.headline: Typhoon Bavi makes landfall in eastern China after 1.7 million are evacuated
items.summary: Bavi came ashore near Taizhou in Zhejiang late on July 11 with winds around 144km/h, after more than 1.7 million people were evacuated in Zhejiang and over 100,000 in Fujian. Taiwan moved 14,000 residents from mountainous areas and cancelled hundreds of flights.

items.headline: US Representative Ro Khanna says Israeli settlers and soldiers detained him in the West Bank
items.summary: Democratic congressman Ro Khanna said armed settlers, later joined by Israeli soldiers, blocked his group for more than an hour near the displaced Palestinian hamlet of Khirbet Zanuta. The Israeli military denied detaining anyone, saying troops dispersed civilians blocking a road.

items.headline: Ukraine chokes fuel supplies to Crimea and Russia to squeeze the military
items.summary: Ukraine's strikes on refineries and depots have caused petrol and diesel shortages across Russia and halted civilian fuel sales in Sevastopol. Kyiv's air force says Russia has lost 42.7% of its refining capacity over the past year.

items.headline: Ollama raises $65 million as its open-source AI runtime nears 9 million developers
items.summary: Ollama, which lets developers run open-weight AI models locally, closed a $65 million Series B led by Theory Ventures, taking total funding to $88 million. The company says usage has doubled since January to about 8.9 million developers and that it is used inside 85% of the Fortune 500.

items.headline: Morgan Stanley warns AI chipmakers' pricing power is fading as the rally cools
items.summary: Morgan Stanley strategist Lisa Shalett urged caution on chip stocks, arguing that hyperscalers designing their own cheaper silicon are eroding pricing power just as earnings estimates hit historic extremes. JPMorgan took the opposite view, calling the recent dip a buying opportunity.

items.headline: AI startup Lyzr lets its own agent run its $100 million fundraise
items.summary: Lyzr said its SivaClaw agent fielded questions from more than 130 investors, drafted memos and tracked which slides backers lingered on while helping close a $100 million Series B at about a $500 million valuation. The company said it drew $400 million in interest without founders touring Sand Hill Road.

items.headline: Microsoft starts replacing OpenAI and Anthropic models with its own AI in Office
items.summary: Microsoft has begun routing a share of Copilot prompts in Excel and Outlook to its in-house MAI models to cut inference costs, though it says OpenAI's frontier models still handle more demanding tasks. AI chief Mustafa Suleyman has said the goal is to reduce reliance on external providers.

items.headline: Delta beats estimates as premium revenue overtakes the main cabin for the first time
items.summary: Delta reported adjusted earnings of $1.56 a share, above the $1.48 expected, with revenue near $19.8 billion. Premium tickets brought in $6.92 billion, edging past the main cabin's $6.85 billion for the first time, and the airline affirmed its 2026 profit outlook.

items.headline: Meta posts its best stock week since early 2024 on AI optimism
items.summary: Meta shares rose about 15% over the week, their strongest since early 2024, after the launch of its Muse Image and Muse Spark models and reports that its custom Iris chip enters production in September. The rally erased the stock's losses for the year.

items.headline: Oil posts a weekly gain of about 6% as Strait of Hormuz disruption persists
items.summary: Brent crude settled at $76.01 a barrel on July 10, slightly lower on the day but up roughly 6% on the week, as renewed US-Iran fighting kept shipping through the Strait of Hormuz near a standstill. West Texas Intermediate ended around $71.41.

items.headline: China sets its yuan fixing below 6.80 per dollar for the first time since 2023
items.summary: The People's Bank of China set its daily reference rate at 6.7989 per dollar, its strongest since February 2023, signalling comfort with a firmer currency. The offshore yuan rose as much as 0.3% to 6.7785 per dollar.

items.headline: 🎾 Noskova beats Muchova in an all-Czech final for her first Wimbledon title
items.summary: Linda Noskova defeated compatriot Karolina Muchova 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 on July 11 for her maiden Grand Slam crown, becoming the youngest Wimbledon women's champion in 15 years. Muchova saved five championship points in the second set before Noskova closed it out in the third.

items.headline: 🎾 Sinner meets Zverev in the Wimbledon men's final
items.summary: World No. 1 and defending champion Jannik Sinner faces Roland Garros winner Alexander Zverev in Sunday's final, their 15th career meeting. Sinner leads the head-to-head 10-4 and has won their past nine matches; the pair have never met on grass.

items.headline: 🏏 Buttler 131 and Brook 95 not out carry England to a 4-0 T20I sweep of India
items.summary: England won the fifth T20I at Southampton by 56 runs on July 11 to complete a 4-0 series whitewash and return to No. 1 in the T20I rankings. Jos Buttler made 131 off 64 balls and Harry Brook an unbeaten 95 off 45 in a stand of 233 as England posted 257 for 3.

items.headline: 🏎️ F1 heads to Spa for the Belgian GP with Antonelli 25 points clear
items.summary: Formula 1 resumes at Spa-Francorchamps on July 17-19 for the Belgian Grand Prix. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli holds a 25-point advantage over his Mercedes team-mate George Russell after Charles Leclerc won the British Grand Prix.

items.headline: Astronomers capture a 'dark' comet growing a tail for the first time
items.summary: A team led by NASA JPL's Davide Farnocchia used the Very Large Telescope to record the first clear image of a tail on a so-called dark comet, published in Nature Astronomy. The finding could help explain the odd, comet-like acceleration of interstellar visitors such as 1I/'Oumuamua.

items.headline: Harvard's silicon chip writes 64 DNA strands at once using electricity and water
items.summary: Harvard researchers built a chip with 256 ring electrodes that drives 64 parallel enzymatic DNA syntheses by tuning the local pH with electric current, avoiding the harsh solvents of conventional methods. As a demonstration they encoded 169 bytes of text as DNA, reported in Nature Electronics.

items.headline: Study finds every pregnancy rewires the brain in its own way
items.summary: A prospective study of 110 women in Nature Communications found that first and second pregnancies leave distinct imprints on grey matter, white-matter tracts and brain networks, with the second fine-tuning changes seen in the first. The authors say the work could improve care for maternal mental health.

items.headline: China's Tianwen-2 returns the first close-up image of Earth's quasi-moon
items.summary: China's space agency released the first close-up picture of Kamo'oalewa, a roughly 40-metre asteroid that shadows Earth's orbit, taken as the Tianwen-2 probe closed to within about 20km. New spectral data have cast doubt on the idea that the body is a fragment of the Moon; samples are due back in 2027.

fun_fact.headline: A hummingbird is the only bird that can fly backwards
fun_fact.body: A hummingbird is the only bird that can fly backwards, using shoulder joints that let its wings pivot in almost a full circle. Its heart races from about 225 beats a minute at rest to more than 1,200 in flight, while its wings beat up to 80 times a second.

puzzle.title: The Census Taker
puzzle.body:
A census taker asks a woman the ages of her three daughters.

The woman says the product of their ages is 36, and their sum is the same as the number on the house next door.

The census taker walks next door, checks the number, comes back and says, "I still can't tell."

The woman replies, "Oh — the eldest is learning the piano."

The census taker now knows all three ages. What are they?
puzzle.approach: Notice which clue only becomes useful once you know it was not enough on its own.
puzzle.answer:
The ages are 2, 2 and 9.

The age triples whose product is 36, with their sums:
1, 1, 36 (sum 38) · 1, 2, 18 (21) · 1, 3, 12 (16) · 1, 4, 9 (14) · 1, 6, 6 (13) · 2, 2, 9 (13) · 2, 3, 6 (11) · 3, 3, 4 (10).

The census taker knew the sum (the house number) yet still could not decide, so the sum must be one that appears more than once. Only 13 does — from 1, 6, 6 and 2, 2, 9. Naming the eldest daughter implies a single oldest child, which rules out 1, 6, 6. So the ages are 2, 2 and 9.

word_puzzle.title: Tail Ends
word_puzzle.body:
Sort these 16 words into four groups of four. Each group shares one hidden second word.

FIRE · KEY · GREEN · DRAGON
WARE · NET · SURF · MAY
LIGHT · BUTTER · DASH · HOME
HORSE · CARD · FARM · FRAME
word_puzzle.approach: Each word pairs with the same hidden second word to form a compound; find the four endings, and watch for words that seem to fit two groups.
word_puzzle.answer:
Add a common second word to each group:

…FLY — BUTTER, DRAGON, MAY, HORSE (butterfly, dragonfly, mayfly, horsefly)
…WORK — FIRE, NET, HOME, FRAME (firework, network, homework, framework)
…BOARD — KEY, CARD, DASH, SURF (keyboard, cardboard, dashboard, surfboard)
…HOUSE — GREEN, LIGHT, WARE, FARM (greenhouse, lighthouse, warehouse, farmhouse)

The traps: FIRE suggests FIREFLY or FIREHOUSE and GREEN suggests GREENFLY, but each group needs exactly four, which forces the split.

UK News ran on fallback sources (Bloomberg): BBC, Sky News and The Guardian were all unreachable/crawler-blocked, and CNN/Al Jazeera had no in-window UK-domestic coverage, so UK carries 3 items (fewer stories today).
